subject: Provisional uptime smoothing and credit escrow proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@stratiform.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional uptime smoothing and credit escrow proposal

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our conversation I pulled together a lightweight SLA proposal that tries to balance predictable economics for Stratiform during ramp with appropriate safeguards for production reliability. High level:

- Baseline hosted availability: 99.9% monthly (standard).
- Option: Dedicated deployment (reserved capacity) can be offered at 99.95% baseline for committed capacity.
- Monthly service-credit cap: we propose a smoothing approach — credits accrue monthly but we cap customer remedy at 10% of monthly invoice and allow a 3-month smoothing window where credits may be applied across the ramp period (i.e., if an early-month incident pushes credit over cap, we can apply forgiveness across next two invoices).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (announced >=72 hours) and emergency maint with postmortems. We propose a 4-hour weekly maintenance window cap by default for hosted.
- Latency SLO: initial target 95th percentile under ~200ms for typical query patterns; we can tighten for Dedicated.

Attachment: SLA_Proposal_StratiForm_v1.pdf (summary + remedy calc examples).

Next steps:
1) Let us know which baseline you expect to buy against (hosted vs dedicated).
2) Confirm whether a temporary elevated credit cap during onboarding (we proposed 10%) is acceptable or if you need a higher safety valve for Q1.
3) If you want, Marcus (legal) and Laura (contracts) will prepare a short redline.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the remedy examples.

—Jordan

From: Alice Monroe <alice@stratiform.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Bob Chen <bob.chen@stratiform.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional uptime smoothing and credit escrow proposal

Jordan —

Thanks for the draft and the clear bullets. A few things on Stratiform's side:

- Production requirement: we run customer-facing inference for live product. We need an operational baseline closer to 99.99% for production traffic; would Redwood consider 99.99% for our production bundle or a tighter remediation ladder?
- Credit cap: 10% is low for our risk tolerance during early ramp. For the first 90 days we would need a monthly remedy cap of 30% (or a written assurance that major incidents will be handled via a separate SLA remediation escrow).
- Latency: 95th under 150ms is our internal target for p95 across typical queries. If Dedicated is required to hit that consistently, call that out.
- Maintenance carveouts: acceptable if scheduled windows are limited and announced at least 48 hours out. Emergency maint: we need a formal post-incident remediation plan and an SLA-grade root cause report within 5 business days.

Can you send redlines and SOC2 evidence? Also please add us to the HubSpot record and send a DocuSign-ready version for legal to review.

Appreciate the flexibility — happy to work through tradeoffs on the baseline vs remedy cap.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Head of Platform Ops, Stratiform Labs
alice@stratiform.com
CC: Bob Chen (Head of Procurement)

Laura / Marissa / Marcus —

Forwarding Stratiform's reply (below). Key asks they put on the table: 99.99% baseline for production, temporary 30% monthly credit cap for first 90 days, p95 <= 150ms, and SOC2 + pledge for RCA timelines. They also want DocuSign-ready papers.

My read: Stratiform is risk-averse during onboarding; they're asking for both a tighter baseline and a higher short-term cap. We can't give 99.99% for hosted without material pricing / capacity commitments. Proposed counter to them:

- Hosted baseline: keep at 99.9% but offer a performance SLA uplift for 'production' traffic if they commit to a 6-month minimum spend or take a Dedicated pool.
- Dedicated baseline: 99.95% by default; we can consider 99.99% for heavy committed commitments (e.g., >$150k/month) but need Legal to quantify remedy exposure and carveouts.
- Credit cap: offer 25% monthly cap for first 90 days (instead of 30%), phasing down to 12% for months 4–6, and then 10% thereafter. Also keep the smoothing across three months but limit aggregated exposure to 45% in any rolling quarter.
- Latency: commit to p95 <= 180ms for Hosted with targeted remediation and p95 <= 150ms for Dedicated.
- Maintenance/RCA: agree to 5-business-day RCA for Sev1s and 72-hour interim update cadence.

Marcus: please review legal exposure with the proposed caps and confirm whether we can accept a 25% initial cap with a rolling quarter aggregate. Laura / Marissa: can you prepare a redline (SLA_Redlines_StratiForm_v2.docx) that codifies the phase-down cap and the maintenance notice windows?

I'll propose a call with Alice next Friday to present the counter.

—Jordan

Alice / Bob —

Thanks for outlining your expectations. We reviewed internally and want to propose a compromise that preserves rollout predictability while addressing Stratiform's early ramp risk appetite. Summary of our revised offer: 

- Hosted baseline: 99.9% monthly. Dedicated baseline (reserved capacity): 99.95% monthly.
- For customers that commit to a 6-month minimum spend (or Dedicated contract), Redwood will provide an optional 99.99% uplift to the Dedicated baseline; uplift pricing to be negotiated.
- Monthly remedy cap: 25% for months 1–3 (initial onboarding), phased to 12% for months 4–6, then 10% standard thereafter. We will cap aggregated remedy exposure at 45% in any rolling 90-day window.
- Latency SLO: Hosted p95 <= 180ms; Dedicated p95 <= 150ms. We will provide trace-level logs for traced requests to support incident analysis.
- Maintenance and RCA: scheduled maintenance requires >=72 hours notice; emergency maintenance will include interim updates within 72 hours and a full RCA within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents.
- SOC2: attached SOC2_Attestation.pdf; full attestation package available on request under an NDA.

Attached: SLA_Redlines_StratiForm_v2.docx (redline), SOC2_Attestation.pdf.

If this structure is acceptable, I'll have Laura and Marcus produce a DocuSign-ready amendment and we can target signatures by Oct 15 to align with your migration window. Otherwise I'm happy to jump on a 30-min call Monday to walk through specifics.

Regards,
